steps.title: Run the Linux ARM64 package
steps.instruction: Unpack the official aerogauge-recomp-linux-arm64.zip and open aerogauge_modern from the extracted folder. The current build needs glibc 2.38, GLIBCXX_3.4.32, SDL2 and a compatible Vulkan driver.

steps.title: Install the official Android package
steps.instruction: Choose aerogauge-recomp-android-arm64.apk from the upstream release. Use an ARM64 device with Android 9 or newer and a compatible Vulkan driver supporting descriptor indexing and scalar block layout.

steps.title: Select your original
steps.instruction: Use the Linux file picker or Android Import ROM with your own matching USA or Japan Rev A cartridge dump. The official package selects the region after checking the ROM. The regions keep separate saves.

warnings: These packages use upstream or player-managed setup, replacement and data backups. Portcove has no native execution or populated-save result for these sibling packages.

references.title: Keep the Linux profile
references.instruction: Preserve $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/AeroGaugeRecomp or ~/.config/AeroGaugeRecomp. If you use the upstream portable.txt mode, preserve the actual program folder and its data.

references.title: Back up Android saves
references.instruction: Use Back up saves in the Android launcher to export EEPROM and Controller Pak files. Keep the exported ZIP separately before changing signing identity, clearing app data or uninstalling.
